name: Founding of Rome
description: Traditional date for the founding of Rome by Romulus and Remus.

name: Roman Republic
description: Establishment of the Roman Republic, marking the transition from monarchy to republic.

name: First Punic War
description: Conflict between Rome and Carthage over control of Sicily, resulting in Rome's victory and acquisition of Sicily.

name: Second Punic War
description: Hannibal of Carthage invades Italy, resulting in major battles such as the Battle of Cannae. Rome ultimately defeats Carthage.

name: Conquest of Gaul
description: Julius Caesar leads the Roman conquest of Gaul (modern-day France).

name: Assassination of Julius Caesar
description: Julius Caesar is assassinated by a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius.

name: Battle of Actium
description: Mark Antony and Cleopatra are defeated by Octavian (later known as Augustus) in a naval battle.

name: Roman Empire
description: Octavian becomes the first Roman Emperor and the Roman Republic transforms into the Roman Empire.

name: Construction of the Colosseum
description: Construction of the iconic Colosseum in Rome is completed.

name: Reign of Trajan
description: Under Trajan's rule, the Roman Empire reaches its largest territorial extent.

name: Conversion to Christianity
description: Emperor Constantine issues the Edict of Milan, legalizing Christianity and promoting religious tolerance.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: The Western Roman Empire collapses due to invasions and internal conflicts.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: The Eastern Roman Empire continues as the Byzantine Empire, with its capital in Constantinople.

name: Sack of Rome
description: The city of Rome is sacked by the Visigoths under the leadership of King Alaric.

name: Coronation of Charlemagne
description: Charlemagne is crowned as Emperor of the Romans by Pope Leo III.

name: Fall of Constantinople
description: The Byzantine Empire falls to the Ottoman Empire, leading to the end of the Roman Empire.

name: Legacy of Roman Law
description: The legal principles and practices of the Roman Empire greatly influence Western legal systems.

name: Revival of Roman Architecture
description: During the Renaissance, classical Roman architecture inspires architectural styles and designs.
